title: Multi-Org: Spot the Duplicate Data 360 Footprint

steps.prompt: Two CRM orgs must share one governed customer lake. Leadership rejected a second full Data 360 home on cost grounds. Click the connection in this provisioning sketch that creates the duplicate footprint.
steps.genericMissCopy: That link can be valid in a multi-org estate. It is not what stands up a second Data 360 home.

hotspots.missRationale: Data 360 B exists because of how Companion is attached. The fault locus is that attachment edge—the pattern that creates the second home.
Two lakes activating into Marketing Cloud is a symptom of dual homes, not the provisioning choice that created the second lake.
Home CRM→Home Data 360 is the intended single home. Removing it does not fix companion sprawl.
The companion CRM is a requirement. It should attach to the shared home, not disappear.

options.label: Data Cloud One onto Home Data 360; retire Data 360 B
options.rationale: Data Cloud One lets additional CRM orgs consume a shared home Data 360 instead of provisioning a separate Data 360 per org.

options.label: Keep both Data 360 homes and sync profiles with nightly files
options.rationale: File sync between two Data 360 homes preserves duplicate cost and drift; it does not meet the single governed lake constraint.

options.label: Merge both CRM orgs into one before enabling Data 360
options.rationale: Org consolidation is a separate program. Multi-org Data 360 sharing is solved with Data Cloud One, not by forcing a CRM merger first.
